claim.summary: For a finite list of real coordinate pairs, if B bounds every residual against a target coordinate, δ bounds every real-part gap below, δ is positive, c is nonnegative, and c > B/(2δ), then every coordinate in the list has strictly smaller shifted squared modulus after the shift.
claim.residual_envelope: forall p in coords, residual a b p <= B
claim.positive_gap_envelope: forall p in coords, δ <= a - p.1
claim.explicit_c_condition: 0 < δ and 0 <= c and B/(2*δ) < c
claim.conclusion: forall p in coords, shiftedSqMod c p.1 p.2 < shiftedSqMod c a b

proves: coordinate-envelope dominance from explicit scalar lower bound c > B/(2δ)
does_not_prove: that the coordinate list is a matrix spectrum

that a strict-abscissa eigenvalue of a real matrix is real
